# Apex Flow 3D Scraper

> Convert accessible public web pages, PDF and DOCX documents into clean Markdown. Hosted API with prepaid credits, or open-source self-hosting. Built by Apex Flow Labs. Engine version 0.2.0; hosted launch 6 November 2026.

## What it does
- Converts pages to Markdown with headings, GFM tables, fenced code with language, absolute links; removes navigation, cookie banners and hidden elements.
- Renders JavaScript pages in an isolated Brave browser, with screenshots on request.
- Reads PDF, DOCX, RSS/Atom feeds and JSON.
- Maps sites (robots.txt, nested and gzip sitemaps), crawls with durable jobs, change tracking with diffs.
- Owned full-text search (SQLite FTS5, BM25) over everything scraped.
- JSON-Schema extraction using DeepSeek first, OpenRouter second.
- MCP tools for agents: fetch, map, crawl, search, compare.
- Obeys robots.txt and Crawl-delay; fetches public addresses only.

## Measured results (30 public URLs, 94 hand-checked reference checks, 5 Nov 2026)
- 26 of 30 URLs fetched; 92 of 94 Markdown fidelity checks passed (97.9%).
- Median 1,454 ms per URL; median process memory 56.4 MB.
- Versus Firecrawl (free keyless tier, same checks, hand-scored) on 24 URLs with references: 91/93 vs 85/93; we score higher on 6 pages, tie on 18, lower on 0. Firecrawl returned content for all 30 URLs; we returned 26 (two blocked by robots.txt that we obey, two by bot walls).

## Hosted service and limits
- Hosted API: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/v1. OpenAPI 3.1: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/openapi.json. Human enrollment: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/trial.html. Free trial: 1,000 credits once, subject to network and daily capacity. Project Pass: $5 once for 5,000 credits valid for 30 days. Monthly plans: $15 for 25,000; $79 for 150,000; $299 for 750,000 credits. Plain pages cost 1, rendered pages 3. No automatic overages.
- Hosted: page scraping, JavaScript rendering, CSS field extraction, batches of up to 10 URLs, sitemap mapping, and account-scoped search over the latest 100 successfully scraped URLs. A nonempty map costs 1 credit; saved-page search costs no credits.
- Hosted responses: 256 KiB per scrape. Two concurrent scrapes per account, subject to shared capacity. Attempts, including failures, are capped at twice the plan's credits per period. Failed scrapes return reserved credits.
- Hosted model extraction and bulk crawl are not included. Those features remain in the self-hosted edition. Documentation: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/docs.html.

## Not claimed
- No CAPTCHA solving or bot-wall evasion; zillow.com and glassdoor.com block it.
- Search covers sites you have indexed, not the whole web.
- We do not claim universal competitor superiority, the lowest price for every workload, or guaranteed availability on every source.

## Agent setup
Official MCP Registry entry: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/io.github.Apexflowlabsllc%2Fapex-flow-web-scraper/versions/latest
Set up Codex CLI, Claude Code or VS Code: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/docs.html#agents
Remote MCP: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/v1/mcp (Streamable HTTP, Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY). Connect a stdio MCP client to the hosted API: https://webscraper.apexflowlabs.com/docs.html#agents. Five tools support scraping, batching, mapping, saved-page search and credit balance. Enrollment requires a human.

## Usage
Python: `from rainbo_scrape import scrape; scrape("https://example.com").markdown`
CLI: `rainbo-scrape fetch https://example.com`

For a smaller REST or MCP scrape response, select outputs such as ["markdown"] or ["data", "evidence"]. Source receipts and validation warnings are retained when available.
